newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE Aug white sugar pushes higher in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE Aug white sugar pushes higher in heavy trade.

text.p: London's nearby August white sugar contract held onto its recent gains and pushed through another resistance point on Thursday in solid early volume, traders said.
August opened slightly above Wednesday's close and then headed up to a high of $316.30, through initial resistance at $315 and targetting $318.00.
"The August is looking very strong...at the moment the market is purely technical in London," said one.
"But I don't think it's going to stay at these levels until expiry as it's largely panic at the moment and people wanting to jump on the bandwagon," he said.

Speculative buying had been mainly responsible for the strength in the spot month over recent days as trade buyers were deterred by the higher levels and content to sell the position outright or the August/October spread.
Crosses on the nearby spread boosted the hefty volume, which stood at 1,325 lots by 1115 GMT, but most of the trade was outright, traders said.
August/October widened to as much as $9.00 after closing at $7.20/90 on Wednesday, as the second-month October contract remained trapped in a 90 cent range.
August was up $1.90 at $316.30, an intraday high, and October was up 20 cents at $307.00.
Traders said the recent spate of physical raws buying had also helped sentiment to firm in London, although the cargoes had already been covered in the futures market.

Russia is said to have bought a substantial quantity of raw sugar during the past two weeks but details are still unclear, although some five cargoes at 25,000 tonnes apiece are thought to have been sold.
Trading in Paris followed a broadly similar pattern although volume was much lighter at 233 lots.
August was also up $1.90 at $316.30 and October down 10 cents at $306.50.
